_comment: SECONDARY DISCOVERY QUERY SET. This is NOT the benchmark. It exists alongside docs/seo/queries.json, which is frozen and must never change.

the_finding_that_seeded_this.method: First Search Console ingest, window 2026-08-09 to 2026-08-15, read as team@vibeops.ca.
the_finding_that_seeded_this.observation: 644 impressions, 19 clicks. Not one of the 48 frozen benchmark queries appeared among the 10 disclosed queries, and not one /what-we-solve/* page appeared in the top 10 pages. The single largest source of exposure was a BLOG POST: /blog/best-ai-tools-for-civil-engineers-in-2026 took 248 of 644 impressions, 39% of the site's entire search exposure, against 206 for the homepage.
the_finding_that_seeded_this.what_it_means: The benchmark was written from our positioning: consultancy-intent phrases like 'ai consultant for engineering firms' and 'custom software for engineering firms'. The demand that actually exists is TOOL-DISCOVERY intent: 'best ai tools for civil engineers'. Those are different searchers. One is looking to hire a firm; the other is looking for a product list, and lands on a blog post that recommends things. Both may be worth serving, but only one of them is currently being served, and it is not the one the site was rebuilt around.
the_finding_that_seeded_this.the_honest_caveat: 19 clicks over 7 days is a small sample and 9 of them are the brand name. This is a hypothesis with one week of evidence behind it, not a finding. It is written down here so it can be checked against week 2 rather than remembered selectively.

purpose: Measure what Google actually associates with each page, as opposed to what we assumed when the benchmark was written. The benchmark for vibeops.ca was built from the site's own positioning and from the vocabulary of 100+ discovery interviews. That is a deliberate bet on intent match over keyword volume, and it is exactly the kind of bet that needs an instrument capable of showing it was wrong.
seeding_rule: A discovery query is added only from EVIDENCE: a query Search Console disclosed for one of our pages, a phrase a real prospect used in a call or an email, or a term a competitor visibly ranks for. NEVER from a guess or a keyword tool. Guessing is what the benchmark already does, and duplicating that here would just produce a second set of zeros with none of the comparability.
how_it_was_seeded: Every entry below is a query Search Console actually disclosed for this property in the week of 2026-08-09. None is a guess. Brand terms and brand misspellings ('vibe ops', 'vipbops') were deliberately NOT added: we already rank first for them, so probing them measures nothing.
rules: Disjoint from the benchmark. verify.mjs FAILS if any active discovery query also appears in queries.json.
Never promote a discovery query into the frozen benchmark. Doing so would retroactively manufacture an improvement out of a query we already ranked for.
Every query records its provenance. verify.mjs fails without it.
Retire by setting status to 'retired', never by deleting the row. The history of what we thought was worth measuring is itself informative.

Results land in the `serp_discovery` source block, never in `serp_probe`. The two are labelled separately in every report because their totals mean different things: the benchmark's totals are a trend series, this set's are not.

status_values.active: Included in discovery-probe.js and probed at the weekly review.
status_values.retired: No longer probed. Kept for the record.
